accessibility.mechanism: button by default; under asChild the replacement child is the host, so an anchor child makes the menu button a native link

to navigate, compose an anchor through asChild: Follow-ups. The anchor is the menu button itself, so nest no Button or second link inside it. href is the destination and the text content is the accessible name; Enter activation, modified click, middle click, context menu, and open in new tab stay native browser behaviour. Do not emulate navigation with a button onClick

an item that performs an action, such as expanding a section, opening an account menu, or running a command, uses SidebarMenuButton without asChild and stays a native button; do not give it href or aria-current

isActive only sets data-active and the active styling; it never adds aria-current. The authored anchor owns current-page semantics: put aria-current="page" on the one link for the page being shown and on no action button. When a router link component sets aria-current itself, the router owns it

SidebarMenuButton does not own application routing and does no client-side navigation. A plain href navigates natively; a router link component that renders an anchor and forwards its props and ref can be the asChild child, and the router owns navigation

the disabled attribute applies to button items only; on an anchor, aria-disabled only adds inert, dimmed styling (pointer-events-none and reduced opacity) and does not stop keyboard activation of an anchor that has an href; the design system adds no disabled-link behaviour and intercepts no link activation, so omit an unavailable link or render a non-navigating placeholder instead of an anchor with href

in the icon-collapsed presentation an anchor menu button keeps its link role, href, aria-current, keyboard focus, and accessible name from its content, so keep the label text inside the anchor; the tooltip prop, which requires a TooltipProvider ancestor, does not replace that name
